conviction_note: Q4 FY26 was pre-guided on 2026-09-03, so the print turns on the first FY27 guide on new CEO Schomburger's first call. Industry evidence points two ways that roughly cancel: beef packer margins turned positive from August (JBS North American beef EBITDA -2.9% July, 0% August, +3.9% September; DTN +$156/hd on Oct 14, eight straight positive weeks), helped by Tyson's own plant closures. Against that, chicken weakened (PPC US EBITDA margin 6.9% vs 8.7% in Q2; boneless breast -32% YoY, soybean meal +20%; placements still +2-3% YoY). The findings sum to +0.4. The scaled number is slightly negative: p_up 48 because the +9.5% 20-day run-up and the positive put skew already hold the beef recovery, and an outside CEO's first guide could be set low. That is offset only partly by this name's habit of rising on prints, 6 of 7 up, including the August miss with a cut. abs_move 5.5 is the 5.32% event-implied move, raised slightly for a first-year guide. Both numbers are close to zero and their signs differ because neither carries much weight.

Management said in August that FY27 should 'look a lot like 2026'. Because the FY27 bar is disputed, the guidance findings are capped small.

findings.finding: Beef packer margins turned positive after Tyson cut about 20% of industry slaughter capacity in August. JBS's North American beef EBITDA margin went -2.9% in July, breakeven in August, +3.9% in September (JBS Q3, reported about 2026-11-09). DTN estimated packer margins at +$156.36/hd on 2026-10-14, the eighth straight positive week. Tyson closed Joslin IL and Eagle Mountain UT, is selling Pasco, is anchoring beef on three plants, and on Nov 9 announced the Allied Beef partnership to restore Amarillo's second shift by summer 2027. Mexican cattle ports are reopening in phases (Douglas Aug 24, Santa Teresa Sept, Columbus Oct 26, Nogales targeted Nov 30). So the FY27 Beef guide should show a materially smaller loss than FY26's $625-775M, against management's August line that beef losses continue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beef guidance was cut three times in FY26 (May, Aug, Sep). The stock rose +7.96% on 2026-05-04 and +2.85% on 2026-08-03 despite the cuts, so the market has looked through beef losses. No FY guide has yet shown beef improving.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is up 9.5% in 20 days and about 15% off its early-October level, and the put skew is positive. If the beef recovery were fully priced, FY27 consensus would have moved up. Instead the only sourced FY27 consensus ($3.73, +6.9%) predates the JBS print and implies roughly flat operating income, consistent with management's 'look a lot like 2026'. A beef guide improving by $300M+ would sit above that.
findings.independence: Separate sources point the same way. DTN packer margins: https://www.dtnpf.com/agriculture/web/AG/news/article/2026/10/14/feedlots-versus-packers (2026-10-14). Tyson's plant restructuring: https://talkbusiness.net/2026/08/tyson-foods-to-close-beef-plants-in-illinois-utah/ . Allied Beef/Amarillo: https://www.drovers.com/news/tyson-foods-restore-second-shift-amarillo-beef-plant-through-rancher-partnership . Border reopening: https://mynews13.com/fl/orlando/ap-top-news/2026/10/26/with-tighter-checks-for-flesh-eating-screwworm-a-border-crossing-reopens . Stephens (via Talk Business, 2026-11-11) says packer fundamentals improved but cattle prices will not stay soft. All are proxies; Tyson has not quantified FY27 beef.

findings.finding: Chicken, Tyson's largest profit pool (about $1.9B of FY26 segment income), is deteriorating into FY27. PPC's US adjusted EBITDA margin fell to 6.9% in Jul-Sep (vs 8.7% in Q2 and 16.9% a year earlier), on July production up 4.7% against a 2.5% plan. Boneless breast is -32% YoY, tenders -49%, wings -28%. Corn is +8% and soybean meal +20% YoY. Broiler placements are still +2-3% YoY through October. USDA lowered its 2027 broiler price projection. Tyson already cut FY26 Chicken from $1.9-2.05B (Aug) to $1.85-1.95B (Sep 3), and analysts cut Q4 Chicken to $432M (-23% YoY). An FY27 Chicken guide well below $1.9B would undercut management's August 'another constructive year'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Chicken guidance raises drove the May 2026 +7.96% reaction (FY26 Chicken went from an initial $1.25-1.5B to $1.9-2.05B). The first sizable chicken guide-down is untested in this window's history; 2025-05-05 (-7.75%) was the last large negative print.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q4 chicken cut is in the estimates (Q4 EPS estimates -29% over 60 days), but the forward bar still leans on management's August 'constructive year' and Tyson's claim that about 75% of chicken income is pull-model and decoupled from commodity cutout. If the market had priced a chicken reset, FY27 EPS consensus would be falling with Q4 rather than standing at +6.9% growth, and the stock would not have run up 9.5% into the print.
findings.independence: PPC Q3: https://finviz.com/news/411800/pilgrims-pride-edges-past-estimates-but-a-second-leg-of-us-margin-compression-is-the-real-story (2026-10-29). NASS hatchery: https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/sites/default/release-files/796138/brls4426.pdf (2026-11-04). Tyson's own Sep 3 chicken cut: https://ir.tyson.com/news/news-details/2026/Tyson-Foods-Updates-Fiscal-2026-Outlook/default.aspx . Offsetting: the JBS article says oversupply may ease, and Tyson says its value-added mix has kept net price up while cutout fell about 45%. Sized net of Prepared Foods (about $1.3B, expected to grow) and of the beef finding above, which offsets it.

findings.finding: Jeff Schomburger, a former P&G sales executive whom JPMorgan called 'unexpected' with 'limited operational experience in the protein industry', took over as CEO on 2026-10-04. Monday is his first earnings call and the company's first FY27 guide, so a conservative first guide or added restructuring is a plausible risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior CEO-transition print in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: The transition is public. What is not priced is how he sets the first bar: the 9.5% run-up into the print suggests the market expects continuity with King's 'look a lot like 2026', not a reset.
findings.independence: Investing.com preview (2026-11-13) flags the first Schomburger call as a key watch item: https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/tyson-foods-faces-earnings-test-as-beef-losses-mount-93CH-5703491 . This is inference, not a document.

findings.finding: The Sept 3 guide that set the reported Q4 was issued with only July and August in hand, and industry beef margins then improved further in September (JBS +3.9% vs breakeven in August). Q4 Beef may therefore land at the better end of the implied $142-292M loss (consensus $217M), putting total Q4 adjusted operating income at or above the $334M guide midpoint. This sits inside the company's guided range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Reported-quarter misses were looked through: the Aug 2026 EPS miss of $0.06 with a revenue miss still drew +2.85%.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus is scattered from $0.59 to $0.75, so no single number holds the September improvement. The quarter is pre-guided, so this is worth little.
findings.independence: Shares the JBS document with the beef guidance finding (https://www.theagribiz.com/international/jbs-us-beef-margins-turn-positive-as-tyson-cuts-capacity/), applied here to the reported quarter rather than FY27. Capped small because the bar is disputed.

findings.finding: Pork faces a weak FY27 setup. JBS USA's CEO said global pork oversupply means a meaningful recovery will likely take several quarters, against Tyson's August line of 'stable pork' helped by lower hog costs. Q4 Pork consensus is only $14.8M (-68% YoY).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pork (about $225M a year) has not been the line the stock traded on in the baseline prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a small segment and analysts already sit low for Q4, so there is little to price beyond a modest FY27 pork range.

findings.finding: FY26 is a 53-week year and the guide was given on a comparable 52-week basis, so reported Q4 (14 weeks) revenue and adjusted operating income will include an extra week, about 1/13 more volume. Headline numbers against estimates that did not add the week will read as a beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior 53-week quarter in the baseline window.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus sources disagree ($0.59-0.75 EPS; revenue $13.88-14.37B), which is consistent with some estimates including the week and some not. Sophisticated holders will normalise it, so it is small.
findings.independence: Same Sept 3 8-K as the reported-quarter beef finding, a different fact in it. Otherwise none.

baseline_tension: The beef-recovery evidence agrees with the 9.5% run-up and is therefore largely in the price. The chicken and new-CEO risks agree with the mild put skew. The net is near zero, and the name's habit of rising on prints is the one thing leaning the other way.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar disputed): FY27 consensus has one dated source ($3.73) contradicted by an undated $4.65, and Q4 EPS ranges $0.59-0.75. The FY27 beef guidance finding was capped from +1.5 to +1.2 and the chicken one from -1.8 to -1.4. The reported-quarter beef finding went from +0.4 to +0.3 (inside the guided range). p_up moved from 47 to 48.
Rule 5 (proxy): beef and chicken rest on peer/industry data (JBS, PPC, DTN, NASS), not Tyson's own FY27 numbers. They stay filed and small; no size change beyond rule 6.
Rule 3 (own caveat): the new-CEO finding is inference; trimmed from -0.5 to -0.4. Pork trimmed from -0.3 to -0.2 because it shares the JBS document and is a small segment.
Rule 9 (segment net): beef and chicken were already sized net of each other and of Prepared Foods; nothing changed.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest is low and the skew mild; the positioning finding (+0.5) stands.
